gloss: to remain unsold; to be left over

definitions.gloss: to remain unsold; to be left over (of merchandise)
definitions.explanation: For goods or products to fail to sell and remain in stock or on display. Often implies that the items are undesirable or that demand was lower than expected.

examples.japanese: ケーキが{売|う}れ{残|のこ}った。
{売|う}れ{残|のこ}った{商品|しょうひん}を{半額|はんがく}にする。
examples.english: To mark unsold merchandise down to half price.

examples.japanese: {大量|たいりょう}に{仕入|しい}れたのに、ほとんど{売|う}れ{残|のこ}ってしまった。
examples.english: We stocked up in large quantities, but most of it went unsold.

notes:
A compound verb combining {売|う}れる (to sell, intransitive) and {残|のこ}る (to remain). Describes merchandise that fails to find buyers and stays in inventory.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {商品|しょうひん}が{売|う}れ{残|のこ}る: merchandise remains unsold
- {在庫|ざいこ}が{売|う}れ{残|のこ}る: inventory is left over
- {大量|たいりょう}に{売|う}れ{残|のこ}る: to have a large amount left unsold
- {売|う}れ{残|のこ}った{品物|しなもの}: leftover goods

RELATED WORDS:
- {売|う}れ{残|のこ}り: unsold goods (noun form)
- {売|う}り{切|き}れる: to sell out — the opposite outcome
- {在庫処分|ざいこしょぶん}: clearance sale, inventory liquidation
